title: Brand Architecture: When Should You Create a New Brand?
seoTitle: Brand Architecture: Models, Examples, and How to Choose | CRUDA
description: See how Amazon, Mercado Libre, BMW, and Marriott organize their brands. Compare four models and decide what fits your business.
html:
Brand Architecture: When Should You Create a New Brand?

How to grow without making your clients have to understand who you are again.

Your company has grown. It does more, takes on different projects, or works in a new market. But when clients recommend you, they describe the company they knew ten years ago. Your team can see what’s changed. Your customers are still catching up.

Then a proposal appears: let's give it another name. Seems like a quick way to show the change. Until someone asks what will happen to everything it cost to build under the previous name.

That is the tension we are going to resolve: how to make the client understand what is new without losing what they already recognize and value.

What is brand architecture?

Brand architecture organizes the names under which a company presents its products and services, and shows how they are related. It helps decide when to share a brand, when to distinguish an offering, and when to build a different brand. The decision depends on what the buyer needs to understand and what the company can sustain. [1]

You don't need to know the models to recognize the problem. In the pages that follow, we'll name them, compare what they allow and what they require, and come back to your company with better questions.

In this article

What does a brand mean and what does architecture organize?
The four models, with advantages and risks
Quick comparison for your business
Amazon and Marriott: combine and reorganize
Design, architecture and luxury: what should be shared
A case of CRUDA and the questions to decide

First: what is a brand?

A brand is a set of meanings that people attribute to a company, a person or something that is offered commercially.

Editorial definition by Fran Herrera for CRUDA.

In simpler terms: it is what a name makes you think and hope. When someone recommends a supplier to you because “it delivers,” that word sums up an experience. If someone else tells you “it's cheap, but you have to be on top of it,” they are also talking about the brand.

The name and logo help identify. What you sell, how you serve, and what happens when there is a problem help form that expectation. You can influence it, but not completely decide what others think.

And what is brand architecture?

It is the way to organize the names with which you present your products and services, and to show what relationship they have. Decide what goes together, what stands out, and what gets support from another brand. [1]

Let's take a hypothetical situation: a company that manufactures windows begins to offer installation. You can call the service “[your brand] installation.” You can give it a different name and clarify who supports it. Or you can create an independent brand. It is a hypothetical example: the three options require explaining what the client contracts and who responds.

Four decisions that are often confused

Brand: what people think and expect from you.
Positioning: what place you want to occupy in the minds and hearts of your customers.
Identity: how you present yourself: name, logo, colors and language.
Architecture: how the names of your different offers are related.

Changing a logo can renew the presentation. It does not decide whether two businesses should share a name. That is why a change of image, by itself, is not a change of architecture.

Parent company and brand: what does the customer need to see?

Before choosing another name, separate two decisions that are often mixed: how you organize the company inside and how you present it to those who buy.

Think about Google, the company you know for its search engine and other services. Since a reorganization announced in 2015, Google has been part of a parent company called Alphabet. A parent company is a company that controls other companies. [2]

When announcing it, Google explained that Alphabet would not be a large consumer brand to bring together its products. The search engine was not renamed “Alphabet Search”. The company was reorganized, without asking the user to learn another name to search for. [2]

A holding is a company that owns shares in other companies. It is used to talk about property. Brand architecture answers another question: under what names are offers presented and how are they related to the customer?

What this means for your business

You can open a company in another country and continue using your brand. You can also have a single company and sell under several names. Legal and business decisions must be coordinated, but they are not equivalent.

The same happens within the company. Having an after-sales manager does not require you to create an after-sales brand. Opening a branch does not require you to name another business. A new name needs a reason that the buyer can understand.

Models are four ways of relating names

A main brand, separate brands, an endorsed brand and a sub-brand. They are reference points: a company can combine several relationships. Let's see what each one allows, what it requires and where it can fail. [1]

1. Main brand: grow with a well-known name.

If the new continues what your customers already value, the familiar name can be a starting point. This is the first alternative.

It is the main brand model, also called branded house. The idea is simple: the well-known name accompanies different offers. Each product may have its own name, but the common brand takes center stage.

Apple sells Mac computers, iPad tablets, and iPhone phones. The buyer can distinguish the products and, at the same time, recognize the same brand behind them. It is a pedagogical reading: product names also have their own force. [3]

What can the company gain?

A new offer can be based on a brand that the customer already recognizes. Part of the communication effort is concentrated and it is easier to show a family of services. For a window company, adding installation under your name can help explain that you offer a complete solution.

What can go wrong

Reputation becomes more connected: a non-compliance in installation can affect trust in the windows. Additionally, if the name means something too narrow, the new activity may not seem credible. Just because they know who you are doesn't mean they consider you capable of doing anything.

Before choosing it: ask what the current name brings to the new offer and what expectation it requires it to meet. If you only bring familiarity, you still need to demonstrate your ability.

2. Independent brands: distinguish proposals.

But sometimes the shared name stops helping: it makes you wait for the same thing where you need to explain an important difference. So it is worth evaluating different brands.

It is known as house of brands or house of brands. The company brings together brands that the buyer can choose separately. The group name does not have to be on the front of each product.

BMW Group is the business group. Within it are the car brands BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce; also BMW Motorrad, for motorcycles. A MINI is not presented to the buyer as “BMW MINI”. The group presents BMW from sportsmanship and Rolls-Royce from luxury and craftsmanship. They share an owner, but they do not seek to arouse exactly the same expectation. [5]

In clothing, Inditex is the group to which Zara, Bershka and Massimo Dutti belong, among other brands. They are stores with their own names and presentations. The comparison with BMW shows that the separation does not respond only to a price scale: it also allows us to distinguish styles and proposals. [6]

What can the company gain?

Each brand can build a more specific personality and offering. It also allows you to preserve the name of an acquired company when its customers already value it. The buyer does not need to learn the entire structure of the group to choose one of its brands.

What can go wrong

Each name needs to become known and sustain a reason for being chosen. That requires resources, materials and management. If two brands offer almost the same thing, they can divide efforts and confuse. Furthermore, separating names does not guarantee isolating problems: common property may be public.

Before choosing it: explain what difference your own brand needs and why a line within the existing brand would not be enough. Having more brands does not, by itself, demonstrate more specialization.

3. Endorsed brand: a name with a reference.

Separating has a cost: some of the familiarity may be left behind. What if the offer needs a proper name, but it also helps to know who is behind it?

An endorsed brand, also called endorsed brand, presents itself with its own identity and shows who endorses it. In English, “by” means “for”: in these names it functions as a visible sign of relationship.

Courtyard by Marriott is a hotel brand. Courtyard identifies the offer; Marriott provides a reference of origin. DoubleTree by Hilton uses a similar relationship: the guest sees a personal name and the link to Hilton. [7][8]

In hospitality, sharing a group does not mean being the same hotel

Marriott International is the hotel company whose suite of brands includes The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W and EDITION, as well as Courtyard. Hilton brings together, among others, Waldorf Astoria and Conrad. Marriott presents St. Regis through refined service and W through design and busy spaces. Both are in luxury: distinguishing brands also allows us to offer different experiences at a high level. [7][8]

For those who book, knowing that they belong to a group can be useful. You still need to understand what experience that hotel offers. Nor does the brand relationship indicate, by itself, who owns the building.

Backup advantage and limit

The advantage: an offer can build its own name without losing all reference to a well-known brand.
The risk: the endorsement generates expectations that must be met. And keeping two names may require more explanation. If the client does not know who they support, that link can contribute little.

Before choosing it: ask what specific question the endorsement solves. Who answers? Where does the service come from? What experience sustains you? The name helps when that relationship means something to the buyer.

4. Subbrand: distinguish without moving away.

There is another possibility: that the client first recognizes the family and then understands what makes each offer different.

A sub-brand distinguishes an offering by maintaining a close relationship with a parent brand. Think of it as a name that allows you to recognize something particular without erasing the family to which it belongs.

Mercado Libre allows you to buy and sell. Mercado Pago offers financial and payment services. Shipping Market brings together logistics services. The company presents them as parts of the same set of services. Names help distinguish tasks and preserve a recognizable relationship. It is an example of a family of names; It does not imply that all three have the same weight or role. [9]

In clothing, Polo Ralph Lauren and Ralph Lauren Purple Label retain Ralph Lauren in their names. Purple Label identifies a luxury offering; Polo has its own proposal. There are differences within a shared universe, without turning each offer into a completely foreign brand. [10][11]

What can the company gain?

It can explain a specialty, line, or level of service while retaining some of the familiarity of the main name. It is useful when the buyer needs to distinguish, but the relationship with what exists still helps.

What can go wrong

If each small variation is given a different name, the customer ends up studying a catalog of labels. It can also be difficult to understand why a line costs more or includes less. The difference has to appear in the product, the service and the commercial explanation.

How is it different from the endorsement? In a sub-brand, the main name is still closely linked to the offering. In a supported brand, its own identity usually has more prominence. There are intermediate zones; It matters what the relationship conveys, not just where the logo is placed. [1]

How to choose between the four models.

Models describe relationships, not steps of maturity. A large company does not need many brands because it is large. A little girl should not wear just one out of obligation. [1]

Comparison of brand architecture models
ModelWhat allowsWhat requires or risks
Main brandSubmit several offers with a known reference.A common expectation that everyone must meet. One problem can affect the whole.
Independent brandsDistinguish proposals and preserve valuable names.Build and manage recognition for each one. You can duplicate efforts.
Endorsed brandGive your own identity and show who is behind it.That the support contributes something and the offer meets that expectation. Two names can be confusing.
SubbrandDistinguish an offer within a recognizable family.Let the difference be clear. Too many labels complicate the choice.

Try it with a concrete decision

Let's go back to the window company. If the facility completes what it already promises, you could present it as a branded service. If you serve a different need, an identifiable line can help. An independent brand deserves study when the current name makes you expect something that that offer cannot or does not want to deliver.

CRUDA's criterion: an internal difference deserves to be visible when something important for the buyer changes. A new supplier, a different margin or a separate team is not enough, on its own, to justify another brand.

Up to this point we saw the alternatives separately. In a real company they can coexist. Amazon shows that coexistence; Marriott, how to reorganize it when the business changes.

Mixed architecture: what Amazon shows.

The question is no longer which of the four models wins. It's what relationship helps in every part of the business. Amazon allows you to see it on a single map.

Amazon is known for its online store, but it also offers music and technology for businesses. In some offers he repeats his name. In others, the client finds a different identity. Looking at both things avoids confusing a large company with a single brand used in the same way.

Amazon Music allows you to listen to music. Amazon Web Services, or AWS, provides computing services over the Internet, such as the ability to store information and run applications. Both retain Amazon in their name. Audible offers audio content and has its own name. They are activities that Amazon presents within its business. [4]

What allows us to observe

Repeating Amazon makes a relationship visible. But it doesn't alone explain why you should trust a company's data to AWS. Each offer needs to demonstrate its ability in its field. Keeping another name allows, in turn, to develop a more specific identity.

The question for your business

If you add an activity, does the current name help the client understand it or does it require so many explanations that it ends up making it difficult? The answer may vary between services of the same group.

For your company, this opens up a possibility: share the name where it helps and keep another where it makes sense. The next question is how to make that change if there are already several names with history.

Marriott: uniting a part without erasing the differences.

When you buy another company, you also receive names that their customers already know. What do you unify without deleting a useful reference? Marriott offers a case: after integrating Starwood, Marriott Rewards, The Ritz-Carlton Rewards and Starwood Preferred Guest, known as SPG, coexisted. There were three loyalty programs, that is, systems of points and benefits for those who book again. [12][13]

Marriott unified the three programs in August 2018. In February 2019, it introduced a common name: Marriott Bonvoy. [12][13]

The hotels retained their different brands. The Ritz-Carlton was not renamed “Hotel Bonvoy.” What was gathered was the relationship of benefits of the traveler with the whole. [7][12]

What problem were you looking to solve?

Marriott introduced Bonvoy as a common way to access benefits and experiences across its hotel portfolio. For the traveler, the name could connect different rooms. For the company, it offered a co-brand for that relationship. That was the announced purpose; does not in itself prove that the name change caused more sales. [12]

What it teaches us and what it demands

Our reading: there is no need to choose between unifying absolutely everything and leaving everything separate. You can unite what the client uses in common and preserve what needs to be distinguished.

The counterpart is operational. A common name requires explaining accounts, benefits and conditions clearly. If the client must figure out how the union works on their own, the rebrand is incomplete.

The change shows where to look before changing all the signs: what can become common and what difference is still useful. In companies where the client buys a creative look, that same question takes on another nuance: does each specialty need a brand?

Does each specialty need another brand?

In architecture and interior design, a client can hire a building, an interior or an object. The order changes, but you can search for the same criteria. Lissoni & Partners and Kelly Wearstler allow us to look at this continuity without confusing it with an identical offer.

Lissoni & Partners: specialties with a visible link

The studio brings together architecture, interiors, product design and visual communication. Their presentation includes Lissoni Casal Ribeiro, Lissoni Associati, Lissoni Design and Lissoni Graphx. The specialty changes; the surname maintains a recognizable relationship. [14]

The reading we took to a lighting client was concrete: a new division does not have to start from an unknown name. You can explain what you do and keep a reference that already helps you understand the criteria of the whole.

Kelly Wearstler: from the interior to the object

Their site features interior projects, product collaborations and a store with furniture, lighting and objects. The name Kelly Wearstler allows you to explore these activities within the same universe. Specific names also appear, such as Side Hustle Gallery; Not everything is reduced to an identical label. [15]

What is useful for a design company: selling an object and developing an interior are different tasks, but they can share a vision. The benefit is recognizing that continuity. The requirement is to demonstrate it in each offer and clarify what work the studio does, what its teams do and what corresponds to a collaboration.

Maps show commercial presentation, not ownership or contracts. Sharing a look does not imply the personal participation of the founder in each assignment.

A broad brand needs to show who knows how to do what.

Keeping a name avoids starting from scratch in each specialty. But it opens up a responsibility: making visible the experience behind each work. That's where the teams and their capabilities matter.

BIG: the client can understand a joint capability

BIG stands for Bjarke Ingels Group, the studio founded by architect Bjarke Ingels. It presents its joint work with the expression BIG LEAP: landscape, engineering, architecture, planning and products. They are different disciplines that are shown within the same study. [16]

The observation that matters: five capabilities do not require building five independent brands. If the client needs you to work together, a common presentation can help explain that collaboration. The limit appears when the breadth makes it difficult to recognize who has the specific experience for each assignment.

Zaha Hadid: the legacy of a name and its limits

ZHA is the architecture office founded by Zaha Hadid. Its history includes CODE, a group dedicated to calculation and design that investigates new ways of designing and building. That specialty can be made visible within the office. [17]

There is an important nuance: Zaha Hadid Design, dedicated to furniture and objects, today belongs to the Zaha Hadid Foundation. The foundation clarifies that the architecture office is an independent entity that operates separately. It is not appropriate to draw them as departments of a single company. [18]

Lissoni, Wearstler, BIG and ZHA leave a useful question: does the client need another name or does he need to see the specialty and those who practice it better? Breadth can help, as long as it doesn't blur what each team knows how to do.

FAENA: what must feel the same when the offer changes?

Showing capabilities solves one part. In luxury it also matters what someone expects to feel when moving from one experience to another. There the relationship between names needs a recognizable intention.

FAENA bears the last name of Alan Faena, an Argentine businessman who went from fashion to hotel and real estate projects, together with partners and collaborators. [21]

The brand allows you to approach hotels, residences and cultural proposals. They are different activities: staying, living and participating in an artistic experience are not the same purchase or the same relationship. The name Faena connects them. [19][20]

What we see from CRUDA

Our reading: Faena brings together art, design and hospitality under a recognizable way of experiencing a place. The surname proposes something that can continue even if the service changes.

Positioning and architecture meet here. Positioning asks what place the brand wants to occupy in the mind and heart. Architecture decides how the names of the offers that seek to build that place are related.

The advantage and the requirement

A common name can help one experience spark interest in another. But that connection is not sustained only by the last name. The care of the space, the attention and the cultural decisions have to give reasons to recognize the same brand.

For a luxury entrepreneur, the question is concrete: if the client moves from one offer to another, what should he continue to feel and what does he need to find differently? This response allows us to evaluate whether sharing the name makes sense, beyond the fact that all offers belong to the same owner.

Faena Art presents itself as a non-profit organization. The map shows a public name and experience link; not a corporate organizational chart or equality of business models. [20]

A CRUDA case: when the name is not enough.

This distinction came about when working with a lighting company. It had grown in services and markets, but the client did not interpret its capabilities in the same way in all of them. In the home market I knew the trajectory and the team. In the new one, he trusted the founder above all.

The company brought together design, product sales and different ways of handling projects. Each activity had an internal logic. Our job was to examine which ones needed a name of their own and which ones could be presented together.

Share, differentiate and demonstrate

Sharing: We proposed to bring together compatible offers under the existing business name. Opening another market did not by itself justify another name. The trajectory could be presented as proof, although recognition had to be built there.

Differentiate: the design studio had to be able to be explained as a service with its own fees. In commercial conversations, the relationship between recommending lighting and selling the products could raise questions about the independence of the advice. A separate identity deserved evaluation, along with the actual conditions of service.

Demonstrate: The founder would retain creative direction and oversight on crucial projects. The content also had to show how the senior designers worked. His ability needed to be made visible to expand confidence in the team.

The question that avoided reducing everything to names

What did the client need to understand better: the difference between services, the relationship between companies or who was going to take charge of their project? Each answer required a different action.

The offer had to be organized and confidence increased in those who delivered it. Another brand, on its own, would not have demonstrated the capabilities of the senior designers or made it clear when the founder would be involved. The architecture had to be accompanied by evidence of the work and clear care agreements.

Anonymized real case, based on CRUDA's experience and documentation. The diagnosis and proposed orientation are described. No implementation results or measured business improvements are attributed.

Do you need another brand? Questions before deciding.

Your company grew, but the client still sees a part. Now you can distinguish if you need to know a capacity, differentiate an offer or understand the relationship between brands.

Another brand or product line?

If you change the size, format, or feature, try a description or line name first. If a core promise changes and the current name makes it difficult to believe, consider another identity. Ask what the buyer interprets.

Does the endorsement help or make the specialty less clear?

Show the same offer with and without the known name. Ask what it does, who it is for, and what the customer expects to receive. If the name gives confidence but hides the specialty, explore a sub-brand or endorsement.

Should the name of an acquired company be changed?

First find out what recognition it has. Do clients ask for it by name? What do they value? What do you think will change with the new owner? You can keep, backup or migrate. Unifying them immediately can erase a reference that still helps sell.

Can we sell at different prices with a single brand?

Yes it can be possible, if the client understands what changes between the offers. Separating can be convenient when expectations are difficult to hold together. There is no price at which another brand becomes mandatory.

Who responds when something goes wrong?

If an offer is presented under several names, explain who is selling, who provides the service, and who assists afterward. A drawing of marks does not resolve a confusing derivation. This clarity is also part of what the customer ends up believing about the company.

Before approving another name, I wrote a sentence: “Today the client believes that we do ___; they need to understand ___; let's demonstrate it with ___.” Then I chose the brand relationship that helps close that distance. The drawing will be clearer when the decision is already clear.

Sources: everyday concepts and examples.

Sources verify names, relationships and announced changes. Comparison of advantages, risks and applications is CRUDA editorial analysis; not a study of commercial results of those companies.

title: Brand Strategy: Marketing Starts Before Launch
seoTitle: Brand Strategy Before Launch: The Liquid Death Case | CRUDA
description: What Liquid Death teaches business leaders about making decisions on product, naming, price, and distribution before running a campaign.
html:
Brand Strategy: Marketing Starts Before Launch

What Liquid Death can teach you about your next business decision, even if you've never seen one of their cans.

The product is finished. The price, calculated. The name, chosen. We have already spoken with suppliers and approved how to sell it. Now we need to get someone to care.

This is where many companies call marketing. They ask for a campaign, a website, or a sales deck that gives people a reason to buy. By then, the decisions that could make the offer more interesting have already been made.

When should marketing start?

Marketing begins at the conception of the business: when you decide who you are going to serve, what you are going to offer and how that person is going to buy and experience it. The brand strategy connects those decisions with the place you want to occupy in their mind and heart. Advertising helps communicate it; It does not replace that work.

Liquid Death, a company that began selling water in cans, allows us to see what changes when someone with advertising criteria participates from the beginning. The question that interests us at CRUDA is what could improve your offer if that look came sooner.

In this article

What is Liquid Death and what does it sell?
The idea of Cessario and brand decisions
Sales, expansion and limits of the case
How to apply it in a traditional company
What to review before the next release

First: what is Liquid Death?

Liquid Death is an American beverage brand. Its name means “liquid death.” It started with canned water and today its catalog includes water, carbonated and flavored drinks, cold tea and energy drinks. To understand its origin, let's stay for a moment with water. [2][4]

Imagine a tall can, with gothic-looking letters and a skull. It might remind you of a beer or an energy drink. However, it contains water. That contradiction is part of the idea: an everyday product presented with an attitude that you don't expect to find there. [3]

Cessario described among his buyers adults who cut back on alcohol and use the drink on social occasions. Our reading: water can participate in that moment without requiring the usual appearance of a water bottle. It changes what someone carries in their hand and how they present themselves with it. [4]

Who is Mike Cessario?

He is the founder and CEO of Liquid Death. He previously worked for years as an advertising creative: his job was to find ways to make other companies' products catch attention and mean something to people. With Liquid Death he was also able to intervene in what was going to be sold and how it was going to be presented. [4]

The difference matters. If you receive a bottle already designed, you can think of a campaign for it. If you come in early, you can also discuss the bottle, the name, where it will be drunk, and what someone will feel when they hold it in their hand.

This is where the reading of CRUDA begins: the container can fulfill a commercial and cultural function in addition to containing a liquid. That possibility is decided before producing the first advertisement.

Why start with an idea that seems absurd?

In your meetings, a proposal may sound sensible because it resembles something you already know. That makes it easier to approve it. You can also make it end up looking like everything the customer already has to choose from.

Cessario proposes deliberately looking for ideas that at first seem absurd to get away from the usual answers. He explained it to Entrepreneur: it is a way of exploring, accompanied by small tests. Not an instruction to execute any occurrence. [3]

The observation that opens another possibility

Cessario's conversation with Jon Evans, on the Uncensored CMO podcast, left an observation that particularly interests us: many companies build the offer, name it, and only then hire an agency to make it interesting. Incorporating people who understand culture and behavior from the beginning opens up other possibilities. That is the starting point of this article. [1]

The translation for an owner is concrete: invite someone capable of looking beyond how it is manufactured, how much it costs and what margin it leaves to discuss the offer. Someone who asks what the person who meets them will understand and what would make them want to get closer.

The idea needs a reason

In our reading, calling water “liquid death” works as an easy-to-recognize contradiction. Humor is not attached to a finished product: it participates in the name and presentation. For another business, that opportunity may appear in service, the way you get paid, or a simpler shopping experience.

A rare idea is worth advancing when it helps solve something. If it only surprises the board and means nothing to the buyer, there is still a lack of strategy.

The question is what business decision can make the offer more valuable before asking a campaign to make it interesting.

What does brand strategy help you decide?

A brand strategy sets the place you want to occupy for people and the decisions you will make to build it. At CRUDA, positioning means what space you want to occupy in your clients' minds and, when you are looking for a deep connection, in their hearts.

Choosing that place has consequences. If you want to be the option that gives peace of mind to a buyer, it has to be evident in how you hire, deliver and respond. If you want to be part of a fun time, you also need to decide how to live that relationship.

Brand strategy decisions before launch
Decisionbusiness questionWhat should I be able to change?
OfferWhat does the client need to solve or experience?Product, scope and experience.
Name and presentationWhat does he interpret when he meets us?How the offer is identified and understood.
Price and accessCan and want to buy it like this?Format, conditions and sales channels.
Test and serviceWhat do you need to verify to trust?Demonstration, attention and ability to comply.

The brand is the set of meanings that people end up attributing to you. The strategy guides the work to build them. Advertising carries messages to the market. They are related tasks, with different scopes.

In Liquid Death, name, can and humor support a recognizable intention. But having someone remember it still doesn't solve whether you find it, buy it, and want to return. To evaluate the case we need to look at what happened in the business.

How much does Liquid Death sell? What the figures say.

There is commercial scale behind the story. The company reported US$263 million in recorded retail sales in 2023. In March 2025 it told Modern Retail that it had reached US$333 million in retail sales by 2024. [5][6]

Retail sales means money paid by buyers in stores. It is not equivalent to the income recorded in Liquid Death or its profit. Distributors and stores also participate in that chain.

MicroVentures, a firm linked to investment in the company, published a different figure for 2024: US$240 million of company income. His post explicitly separates that revenue from the $333 million retail. It is reported information, not an audited financial statement that we have reviewed. [7]

And the headlines' $1.4 billion?

It was the valuation announced in a March 2024 financing: how much the company was valued in that operation. It wasn't annual sales or money earned. [5]

This data supports that Liquid Death went much further than a known occurrence on the internet. They do not allow us to calculate how much of the sales were caused by the name, the packaging or each campaign. They also do not prove profitability. The useful question is what decisions made it possible to compete on that scale.

It started with water. The brand could tell something more.

If a company's entire difference depends on a feature that someone else can copy, the advantage is exposed. The example of aluminum, taken up in that conversation, makes it simple: another company can also sell canned water. The brand needs to build something that people associate with it.

In a 2024 interview, Cessario described how Liquid Death went from water to carbonated and flavored drinks and then to iced tea. Their aspiration was to grow in several categories, that is, in different types of drinks. The current catalog also includes energy. [4][2]

Andy Pearson, creative manager of the brand, explained that his team seeks to make people laugh using situations and codes from popular culture. That criterion guides experiences and products in addition to videos. [9]

What is preserved when the product changes

Our reading is that the humor and attitude allow us to recognize Liquid Death even if what is inside the can changes. The promise is not contained in a single characteristic of water. There is a way of introducing yourself that can continue.

For a traditional company, this forces you to think about what your name means beyond the product you started with. A manufacturer may be known for a material, or for its ability to solve a class of projects. That meaning conditions how your next offer will be understood.

There is also a limit: a well-known brand can spark interest in something new, but it does not guarantee that that product will be liked, will have an appropriate price, or will be purchased again. Familiarity opens up a possibility; each offer has to earn its place.

Creativity also has to learn from the market.

History becomes more useful when we stop telling it as an inevitable victory. The same presentation that attracts attention can make someone not understand what they are buying.

In 2025, Marisa Bertha, Liquid Death's chief strategy officer, explained that some people were confusing their drinks with alcohol. He also described smaller cans, new packaging and graphic changes to make it more obvious what each product contained. [6]

Our reading: preserving a personality does not require preserving every initial decision. To reach new consumption situations, it may be necessary to change the format, the entry price or the clarity with which you explain the offer.

A strong brand does not make the product invulnerable

BevNET reported, citing NielsenIQ, a 17.8% drop in dollar sales of Liquid Death's still water line in the 52 weeks ended March 7, 2026. It is a data point for that line in the cited measurement; not of the company as a whole. [10]

It does not allow us to conclude that the entire strategy has failed. It does avoid presenting previous growth as a guarantee of what is to come. We do not locate a verifiable 2025 annual closing of total sales or public audited statements sufficient to affirm its profitability.

What we’d apply to your company

Defend what makes the brand recognizable and review what makes it difficult to understand, buy or use it. They are different questions. A successful campaign does not eliminate a price objection, a bad experience, or a product that is no longer of interest.

The 2026 data is preserved with its specific scope. It is not combined with total sales from other years to draw a group trend.

What can a company that does not sell water learn?

Let's get back to your business. You may sell materials, professional services, or industrial maintenance. You don't need to be like Liquid Death to take advantage of observation: there are pre-campaign decisions that change the value of what you offer.

A hypothetical example: industrial maintenance

The company is preparing a new service. It organizes it by tasks: inspection, spare parts and visits. The budget is ready. Marketing is charged with making it attractive.

Now let's move that conversation forward. A plant manager could explain that their biggest concern is stopping production and not knowing who will respond. It would still need to be investigated: it is a hypothesis about the buyer, not a finding from a CRUDA client.

If that concern is confirmed, the offer could change: emergency care, spare parts available, a responsible person and clear response conditions. Costs, coverage and price would also change. The promise would have a structure to be fulfilled.

The company could aspire to take the place of a trusted partner when the operation is under pressure. Your advertising would have concrete evidence to show: how you work, who responds, and what the contract includes.

That translates Cessario's criteria to a very different business. Creative opportunity appears by looking at the customer's situation while it is still possible to design a better response.

Finding it and buying it are also part of the strategy.

An offer can be of interest and still lose a sale because it is not available when needed. That's why the place where you sell deserves to enter the brand conversation from the beginning.

In 2021, Live Nation, a company that organizes concerts and operates entertainment venues, announced Liquid Death as exclusive water at many of its venues and festivals in the United States. That relationship put the product in situations where it could be consumed, as well as seen. [8]

In 2025, Liquid Death announced new agreements with distributors on the US West Coast. Behind the humor there was a very specific task: getting drinks to the points of sale. [11]

Translation to a service business

In the industrial example, promising a response is of little use if the customer does not know who to call. In a materials company, showing a product may not be enough if an architect does not obtain samples or information to incorporate into a project.

The opportunity may be in making it easier to request a quote, check a capacity, purchase an initial quantity or get support. They are commercial and operational decisions that also form perception.

Should Marketing decide everything?

No. Management, operations, finance, sales and marketing have different responsibilities. The contribution that we defend is that the client's perspective can modify a decision, not limit itself to receiving it to communicate it.

In a small company, this work can be done by the owner with his team and an external partner. The decisive thing is when that perspective participates and what can change, not the job title or the size of the department.

What to review before the next release.

You don't need to remake the company. Choose an upcoming offer: a service, a line, a branch or a new way of contracting. Review it while there are still open decisions.

1. What changes for the client?

I described a use or purchase situation. What are you trying to solve? What bothers you about how you solve it today? What do you expect to feel? It will separate what you heard from what you assume. Our 5 Cs research crosses culture, context, category alternatives, company capabilities and buyer perspective.

2. What place do we want to occupy?

Define with common words what you want the person to think and feel when they meet you. Then explain what product, service, price, name and experience decisions can build that place. “Leading” does not describe a customer experience.

3. What can we demonstrate and maintain?

Check who delivers what was promised, with what resources and under what conditions. If an idea requires a response that the company cannot provide, adjust the offer before turning it into a message.

4. How do we test before committing?

Show an understandable version to relevant buyers: a test packaging, a service proposal or a purchasing journey. Observe what they understand, what they doubt, and what they would do next. When feasible, try an actual purchase on a small scale. Just because an idea is liked does not prove that someone is going to pay for it.

A useful review ends with a decision: change something, prove a specific doubt, or move forward because the evidence is sufficient. The goal is that the research can influence the business before the campaign has to explain everything.

Frequently asked questions: bringing the idea to your company.

Are marketing and advertising the same thing?

No. Marketing includes understanding the buyer and working on the offer, price, access and experience. Advertising communicates through advertisements. It can generate interest and help build brand, but it does not replace the ability to deliver what is promised.

Do I need a provocative idea to differentiate myself?

No. The provocation makes sense within Liquid Death's criteria. In your business, a valuable difference might be clarity, an easier way to hire, or a better-designed service. The question is what matters to the buyer and how do you make it recognizable.

What if my business is already up and running?

Each new offer reopens decisions. You can also review an existing one where doubts, objections or purchase difficulties are repeated. Keep what customers value; Investigate what prevents them from understanding or using the rest.

What does the Liquid Death case prove?

It shows a company that incorporated creative judgment into product naming and presentation, grew in retail sales, and expanded its offering. It does not prove that copying their humor produces the same result or that their sales figures equal profits.

How do we know if we are improving?

See if the customer understands the offer, considers it, buys and returns; Also review costs, margin and delivery capacity. Compare periods or tests taking into account changes in price, distribution and execution. Reactions to a campaign are only one part.

Go back to the meeting we started with. Before saying “now we lack marketing”, ask: what would we change if we thought about how the client is going to choose us while we are still designing the business? There the brand strategy has room to work.

Sources and scope.

The interviews confirm statements; the communications, data reported by the company. The translation to the employer and the decision criteria are CRUDA analysis. Commercial causality is not attributed to an isolated piece or decision.

title: How Do You Get Customers to Ask for Your B2B Brand by Name?
seoTitle: How to Get Customers to Ask for Your B2B Brand | CRUDA
description: See how Intel, Dolby, GORE-TEX, and AGP sGlass make their value visible when other companies sell or integrate their products.
html:
How Do You Get Customers to Ask for Your B2B Brand by Name?

Your company has experience and capabilities. The challenge is for the buyer to understand what those capabilities do for them and can ask for your brand by name. A real question we explored while preparing a proposal for AGP sGlass México.

A proposal lands on the leadership team’s desk. It lays out what to publish, where, and when. The question comes before any of that. How will this help buyers understand our value and ask for our brand?

That was the question we explored while preparing a proposal for AGP sGlass México. A company may know its product very well and have strong relationships in its industry. Still, you need to explain your difference to those who influence the next purchase. That distance is the topic of this article.

How is preference built for a B2B brand?

For a buyer to ask for your brand, they need to understand what difference it makes, verify that this difference is real and know how to achieve it. When you sell through distributors or other companies, you also need them to be able to explain and deliver that value. Communication helps connect those parts; by itself it does not guarantee the election.

B2B means that one company sells to another company. It can be glass for an armored vehicle, an engine for a factory or cement for a construction company. Behind every purchase there are still people who need to choose and be responsible for that decision.

In this article

The problem of AGP sGlass Mexico
Who decides and what needs to be understood
How to make a difference visible and verifiable
How to apply AGP sGlass
Do we also need mass recognition?
What to check in your company

A question we explored in a proposal for AGP sGlass México

AGP sGlass manufactures protective glass solutions. The case of this article corresponds to AGP sGlass México, not AGP Group. Its civilian armor business includes materials for vehicles: one part of a system that must protect its occupants. For this article we focus on that business in Mexico, not on all the group's activities. [1]

In our proposal work for AGP sGlass México, the problem was specific: how to get more buyers to know the differences in their glass and request the brand when ordering shielding. That meant reaching those who decide or recommend, in addition to accompanying the armorers who buy and integrate the product.

The task required connecting communication and business: who we would help, what they needed to understand and how we would facilitate their decision. There were technical skills to explain and experience to share. The challenge was to translate that value into a reason that the buyer could understand and convey.

The buyer does not necessarily buy directly

A armorer is a company that prepares a vehicle to protect those who travel in it. You buy components, integrate them and deliver the work. Whoever orders that vehicle can choose the armor without knowing who manufactured each material.

There appears a question that surpasses the sector: how can a brand matter in the decision when it is part of something that another company sells?

Reputation among those who already work with you does not explain, by itself, what someone who does not yet know you understands.

CRUDA’s proposal for AGP sGlass México. No implementation results are presented nor private exchanges reproduced.

Who has to order your brand?

Before choosing a message, it is advisable to follow the purchase journey. In the same operation there may be someone who recommends, someone who pays, someone who installs and someone who uses the product. They don't always look for the same thing or need the same explanation.

The AGP sGlass proposal included dealers, security managers and buyers of vehicles to be armored, in addition to the armorers themselves. A dealership sells vehicles. A security manager evaluates needs and risks. The armorer does the job. A person can fulfill more than one role; The map is used to investigate, not to assume a single route.

Being known and being asked for are different things.

To recognize a name is to know that it exists. Preferring it is leaning toward it among alternatives. Asking for it is taking a specific step: mentioning it in a query, including it in a quote, or requesting that it be used in a project.

If you sell materials for a project, your first objective may be for the architect to include them in the project. If you sell industrial equipment, maintenance may recommend your service. You don't need to be famous to everyone: you need to make sense to those who influence that purchase.

Before we decide how to reach those people, we need to understand what they lack to choose from. The company may be thinking about communicating more technology while the buyer is trying to solve a much simpler question.

What does the buyer need to understand to choose?

Imagine someone orders an armored vehicle. You can trust the company doing the work and still not know what to ask about its components. It is a possible situation that we need to investigate; not a conclusion about all AGP sGlass clients.

If that were the difficulty, repeating that a manufacturer has experience would not be enough. The person should be helped to recognize what differences matter, where to check them, and how to request them in their budget.

The question that changes work

Instead of starting with “what do we want to say about ourselves?”, we start with “what is this person trying to solve and what are we not understanding about their experience?” The answer may change the message, the evidence we show, and who we need to involve.

At CRUDA we call insight a hidden truth from the client's perspective that, when made visible, allows us to understand something that we did not see before. It can be something everyday that that person experiences without having put it into words. Julian Cole describes it as a revealing truth that changes our reading of the problem. [9]

It is not enough to write a sentence that sounds profound. You have to listen to specific purchases, observe what happened and contrast the interpretation. Nor does finding an insight guarantee sales: understanding and executing are related jobs, with different demands.

Now yes: what the examples teach us

The next three cases help us think about how to explain a difference once we understand the buyer. Intel makes a piece that was inside recognizable. Dolby allows you to experience a capacity. GORE-TEX connects a material with a promise and a support. Each one solves a different part of the problem.

How to make visible what the client does not see? Intel.

Intel is a company that manufactures chips, small electronic parts. One of its products is the processor: the part that executes instructions for a computer to work. In this simplified route, Intel sells those components to equipment manufacturers; the user buys the finished computer. Dell, HP and Lenovo offer computers with Intel processors. Not all of their models use the same chip manufacturer. [10]

Intel was already well-known among manufacturers, but many people outside the industry didn't understand what a processor was or why it mattered who made it. In 1991 it launched Intel Inside, which means “Intel inside.” The name and label helped identify the component within the equipment. [2][3]

The campaign combined its own ads with financial support for manufacturers that incorporated the brand in their products and advertising. There was a reason for those companies to participate: Intel's name could also help them explain the value of their computers. [2]

What we can learn

Our reading: the buyer could begin to recognize a component without becoming an engineer. The brand gave him a reference to ask and compare. The lesson for an industrial company is to find what part of its work deserves to become understandable before the purchase.

For AGP sGlass, the equivalent question is what someone who orders shielding would have to understand for the name of the glass to matter in their decision. Intel shows the mechanism; does not authorize copying a label. First you have to give it a meaning that the buyer and the armorer can explain.

How to prove the difference? What Dolby shows.

Maybe you saw the word Dolby when starting a movie or looking at the features of a television. Dolby develops sound and image technologies that other companies incorporate into their products and services. You don't need to buy a “Dolby brand” movie to find it.

Dolby Atmos is a sound technology that can give the sensation that what you hear is coming from different directions. Dolby Vision works on the image. Netflix offers certain titles with these technologies, when the plan and equipment allow them to be played. They are not available in the same way in their entire catalog or on any television. [5][6]

A difference that can be experienced

Imagine listening to a rain scene. You can explain for several minutes how the audio is processed. Or you can make the person hear the difference with a well-prepared demonstration. This is our reading of the case: experience can help you understand something that a list of specifications leaves behind.

That has a direct translation for other businesses. A window supplier could show how the noise changes with a comparable test. A lighting company can show what the same surface looks like under two solutions. These are application examples, not results attributed to Dolby.

If your difference can be seen, heard, or experienced, ask yourself why you are only describing it.

Back to AGP sGlass: a technical difference needs proper proof. Some properties can be explained with comparisons; others require specialized testing and documentation. The task is to help understand what each test demonstrates. GORE-TEX allows you to see how an everyday promise and its support are connected.

What backs up the promise? The GORE-TEX lesson.

GORE-TEX is a brand of material technologies used in clothing and footwear. Among their products there are very thin layers that are incorporated into a garment or shoe to prevent water from passing through and allowing moisture vapor to escape. The manufacturer of the garment and the technology it incorporates may have different names. [7]

For example, Adidas sells certain models with GORE-TEX. You buy an Adidas product that incorporates that technology; It doesn't mean that all Adidas shoes have it. [8]

GORE-TEX explains that its brand also represents a quality control system. Their promise to keep you dry has a limited warranty on the products covered. There are different conditions and lines: it is not appropriate to extend that guarantee to any product related to Gore. [7]

Translate without deleting the test

For those who go out for a walk in the rain, understanding what the material is for is more immediate than knowing its composition. Our reading is that an everyday promise and an identifiable endorsement work together. Simple language opens the conversation; The details allow you to evaluate whether the offer corresponds to what you need.

In a technical company, translating is not about replacing a report with a slogan. It is to help the buyer understand what problem that report addresses, what it demonstrates and what its limits are.

For AGP sGlass, learning is accompanying each argument with its meaning and evidence: what changes for those who use the vehicle, what supports it and under what conditions. Knowing a brand can spark interest; understanding and verifying its contribution allows it to be evaluated. We can now return to the purchasing journey.

Let's go back to AGP sGlass: how does that value reach the customer?

The initial question begins to have a concrete answer. AGP sGlass needs those who influence a shield to understand their input and be able to request it. At the same time, the armorer must be able to explain that contribution within the complete work that is delivered.

Our recommendation is to work on both sides of that relationship: help whoever chooses to ask better questions and give the business partner useful arguments and evidence to answer them. The experience of leaders and specialists can make that explanation closer.

Make visible the criterion that already exists

An executive can explain what questions to ask before choosing, what differences deserve attention, and what a buyer can check. You can tell how a decision is made without revealing confidential information. This content allows someone who does not yet know you to come closer to your way of thinking.

Our recommendation is to connect each explanation with evidence that the team and partners can also use. A clear guide, a demonstration, or a well-documented case should serve even if the director is not present in that conversation.

The personal voice can open a door. The rest of the company has to be able to sustain what is said: technical knowledge, attention, documentation and monitoring. If everything depends on the executive responding to each message, there is still work to do.

Up to this point we are talking about facilitating a specific decision. But in a management meeting another question may arise: what if we also need more people to know our name before needing the product? That's where Aramco and Globant come in.

Do we need to be known outside the industry?

Sometimes a company also seeks to build familiarity with a broader audience. Aramco serves to distinguish that task from getting someone to order a specific component.

Aramco is a Saudi Arabian energy company. Works with oil, gas and chemicals. Let's take a part of your business: you sell refined fuels wholesale to companies that market them and to industrial customers. Refining means transforming oil into usable products, such as fuel. [15]

In 2020 it announced a global sponsorship of Formula 1, the international motorsport championship. A sponsorship allows a brand to be associated with the event in exchange for agreed upon resources and rights. Whoever sees Aramco in a race does not therefore become a wholesale fuel buyer. [11]

Why appear in front of so many people?

Our reading: business and communication can have audiences of different sizes. Aramco can sell to organizations while seeking familiarity with its name among a broader audience. The F1 environment also allows us to talk about engineering and performance; The announcement included technological collaboration goals. [11]

That's different from Intel Inside. Intel identifies a part of the computer you buy. Aramco sponsorship makes a company visible in a show that you follow. It does not demonstrate purchasing preference or business results on its own.

For AGP sGlass, this forces us to choose priorities: is the obstacle that the right buyers do not know the brand, or that they know it but do not understand what it brings? The answer defines where to invest. The size of another company's sponsorship doesn't answer that question.

Can visibility show capability? Globant.

Globant provides a nuance: presence in a known setting can also coexist with visible technical work. Born in Argentina, she develops digital programs and experiences for other organizations. The organization commissions the work; Your employees or clients use the result.

F1 is a documented example of an organization he works with. In 2024 they announced an agreement for digital experiences. In May 2026, Globant reported on its work on the official F1 app for those attending races. The announcements do not publish the financial conditions of the agreement. [12][16]

Sponsorship is another relationship

Franco Colapinto is an Argentine pilot. In 2023, Globant announced its support for the driver's debut in Formula 2 in 2024. In August 2024, it also announced an alliance with Williams, the team with which Colapinto went on to race in F1. Driver, team and championship are different links. [13][14]

Our read: Globant can showcase its capabilities through the work it does and build familiarity through its brand associations. An amateur can know it without being its client; Anyone who buys technology for a company can also be a hobbyist.

For AGP sGlass, the lesson would be to choose spaces where its knowledge is useful and relate that presence to accessible evidence. Familiarity can open up the conversation; The buyer still needs to evaluate the offer and find someone to deliver it. That is why the next step returns to a specific purchase, not to choosing a sponsorship.

How to bring it to your company?

Choose a specific purchase that you want to understand better. A work, the renewal of a contract, the choice of a supplier or an order that arrived through a distributor. Avoid starting with “our customer” as if everyone buys the same way.

How to review a B2B purchasing decision
What to checkSpecific questionWhat to do with the answer
The purchaseWho recommends, pays and uses?Choose who we need to explain best.
The differenceWhat changes for that person?Translate capabilities into understandable consequences.
The testWhat do you need to check?Gather relevant demonstrations, documents or cases.
accessHow can you order from us and get from us?Agree on route and response with sales and partners.

You can start with conversations about recent trades: one you won, one you lost, and one that was delayed. This selection serves to explore questions, not to statistically represent the entire market.

Ask what happened: who proposed the options, what was worrying, what information was missing, and what advanced or slowed down the decision. I asked for examples. “We value quality” says little until you understand what quality means to that person and what allowed them to recognize it.

Contrast those answers with sales, service, and distributors. If an interesting explanation appears, also look for cases that contradict it. A phrase that we like is not yet a confirmed truth.

When is it appropriate to invest in what they ask you for?

It's a good idea to explore this strategy when your brand choice may matter to the buyer, there is a difference you can demonstrate, and there is a way to request and get your offer. The examples above show possibilities; They do not force every industrial company to do massive advertising.

If the decision occurs between specialists

Perhaps the best job is helping architects, engineers or purchasing managers evaluate your solution. You may need clear documentation, samples, training or detailed cases before a general public campaign. Being easy to recommend in a technical conversation also counts.

If the buyer wants your product, but can't find it

The priority may be availability, budget, installation or dealer response. More interest alone does not fix those problems. Check where the route cuts off before expanding communication.

If you still don't understand the difference

There is a task of explanation there: what changes for that person, how it is tested and why they should care. You can try out a guide or demo with real buyers and see what they understand without help.

How to evaluate if we are making progress?

Record the starting point. See if queries appear that mention the brand, if it is included in quotes, and if partners can explain its value. Review opportunities and reasons for choosing or discarding along with sales. They are signs to learn; They do not alone prove that the content caused a sale.

A business-wise review requires agreeing on what we are going to look at and recognizing what else has changed over that period: pricing, availability, competition and business activity.

Let's go back to the direction question.

“How do we get them to order our brand?” It seems like a communication question. When working on it, it forces us to look at what the buyer understands, who advises them, how they recognize a difference and what happens when they try to buy.

The journey leaves us with three tasks: that the difference is understood, that it can be verified and that there is a clear way to request it. Broad visibility can accompany them when there is a reason to invest in it. It does not replace any of the three.

For AGP sGlass México, our proposal is based on its capabilities and the experience of its team, but it has to reach the buyer's decision. The goal is for someone to be able to understand, explain and request that value, even when there is no company representative in the conversation.

A question for your next meeting

Take a recent business proposal and ask the team: “If the client had to explain why they were considering us to someone who wasn't in this meeting, what could they say and what would they back it up with?”

If the answer requires you to explain everything again, you already have a place to start.
